children.text: Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos (ICAIC)

follows an ICAIC mobile cinema unit as it travels to the rural community of Los Mulos, near Baracoa, to screen a film for residents who had never before experienced cinema. Before the screening, Cortázar interviews members of the community about what they imagine cinema to be. The film culminates with a screening of Charlie Chaplin’s
(1936), focusing on the spectators’ expressions, laughter, and reactions as they encounter moving images for the first time.

is one of the most iconic documentaries of early revolutionary Cuban cinema and a key record of ICAIC’s Mobile Cinema program. The film reflects the institution’s effort to expand access to cinema beyond Havana and other urban centers, particularly into isolated rural communities. By making spectatorship itself the subject of the documentary, Cortázar also captures an important ideal of early ICAIC: cinema as a cultural form that could reach new publics across the island and participate in the broader transformation of Cuban society.

title: Por Primera Vez de Octavio Cortázar (1967)
